A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study of model complexity, double descent and OOD detection. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated theoretical results and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments across CNN, ResNet-18, ViT and Swin architectures, including OOD detection results, width sweeps and neural-collapse analyses in Section 5 and Appendices D–E.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds Gaussian simulations, ResNet-34 experiments, direct OOD-risk measurements and noiseless controls.

M1.justification: The feature-subset least-squares estimator and NC1 under/overparameterization ratio remain unchanged. RRF and ResNet-34 are additional experimental model configurations; the stronger wording about an NC-based selection criterion does not introduce a different algorithm.

E1.justification: The real-image dataset coverage is retained. Section 5.1 and Appendix D.1 add a controlled binary task using GMM-generated samples fitted to two CIFAR-10 classes and separately generated Gaussian OOD inputs.

E2.justification: The evaluated detector set remains MSP, MaxLogit, Energy/ReAct, KL-Matching, Mahalanobis, Residual, ViM, ASH-P and NECO. Matched benchmark plots and Tables 1–2 retain their comparison methods; additional citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds substantial experimental protocols: RRF widths from 2 to 10,000 with 600 training epochs and generated datasets, ResNet-34 evaluations, noiseless controls alongside the retained 20% label-noise setup, and direct OOD-risk evaluation. Existing neural-network training settings are largely retained.

E4.justification: Appendix D.6 adds controls testing whether double descent persists without label noise. Appendix D.1 adds confidence-score histograms examining failure near interpolation, and Figure 22 extends the NC1 analysis to ResNet-34. These provide substantive new robustness and mechanism analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions state five runs with different random seeds and retain variation bands and standard-deviation reporting for the matched experiments. No revised run count, confidence-interval procedure or significance-testing practice is reported.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 2 are numerically unchanged. Added findings include approximately chance-level toy-model AUC near interpolation, ResNet-34 results, empirical OOD-risk curves and noiseless curves showing plateaus instead of the noisy-setting dip. These are additional results under additional protocols.

T1.justification: v2 replaces Taylor approximations with mean-value-theorem arguments and secant-based matrices, revises the activation/covariance assumptions, and adds Lemma 1.1. It also changes the multiclass risk definition and the main OOD upper bound's noise term to 2σ′², although Appendix A.2 retains σ′². Section 4.1 reverses n ≪ d to n ≫ d while retaining full row rank.

C1.justification: The central claims about double descent and the conditional benefits of overparameterization remain. v2 explicitly frames them around post-hoc semantic-shift detection, promotes the existing NC ratio as a regime-selection criterion, and removes the risk metric as a separately listed contribution. The conclusion drops v1's strong claim that improvement occurs only with improved NC convergence.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation of interpolation failure through indiscriminate ID/OOD confidence and identifies noiseless behavior as an important boundary. Its main NC discussion replaces stronger guarantees with tentative associations requiring broader validation. The limitations more explicitly address post-hoc detection, width-based complexity and simplified theoretical models.

D1.justification: Appendix D.1 adds RRF construction, sigmoid output, synthetic-data generation, sample counts, width ranges and training duration. Existing Appendix B settings are largely retained. The promise to release code upon publication disappears from v2; neither PDF supplies code-access instructions.

R1.justification: v2 acknowledges Fang et al. (2024) for closely related OOD-risk formulations and adds semantic-shift, open-set, random-feature and neural-collapse references. Some LLM and application-motivation citations are removed. The basic positioning relative to post-hoc detection and double-descent research remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, NC discussion and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Prediction-risk material moves from the main theoretical section to Appendix A.1, and the experimental narrative is reorganized around the toy example and expanded appendix analyses.

P2.justification: v1 Figure 1's eight separate accuracy/AUC panels become four dual-axis panels in v2 Figure 2. Numerous new experimental figures are added, the NC1 plot gains ResNet-34, tables are resized, and appendix figures are regrouped. Existing eigenvalue and activation visualizations are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: The noiseless controls and direct OOD-risk experiments strengthen empirical assessment and expose a boundary that v1 did not evaluate. Clearer scope and more cautious NC interpretation also help. However, the theoretical revision retains conflicting upper-bound terms and introduces an n ≫ d/full-row-rank contradiction, while the code-release promise disappears. These tradeoffs limit the overall gain.
